anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly: The optimizer relies on stale, incomplete, or misleading statistics, which drives systematic cardinality misestimation and chronic selection of sub-optimal execution plans.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly: Excessive concurrent access to a small set of buffer-cache pages or latches forces sessions to wait or spin, producing high buffer-busy and page-latch latency even when overall memory is sufficient.

When both anomalies surface together, the database experiences a feedback loop where poor plan choices amplify low-level cache and latch congestion, and the resulting contention further increases plan instability and statistics staleness. Observable symptoms include:  • Extreme divergence between estimated and actual row counts combined with surges in buffer_busy, page_latch, or latch_free waits.  • Queries that oscillate between different bad plans after bulk loads or partition swaps, each rapidly throttled by latch waits on hot index roots or data pages.  • CPU saturation due to spin-loops alongside I/O bursts from repeated buffer evictions, paired with sudden plan recompiles and escalating query latencies.  • Monitoring views show both outdated statistics timestamps and hot-page contention on the very objects whose statistics are stale.

Causal chain: stale or inaccurate statistics cause the optimizer to favor access paths (e.g., nested-loop lookups, under-parallelized scans, or monotonically growing index inserts) that hammer a narrow set of pages. This concentrates read/write traffic, increasing latch acquisition frequency and buffer churn. The resulting contention elongates statement runtimes, delaying maintenance tasks such as auto-statistics refresh and check-point driven flushes, which keeps statistics stale and dirty pages resident longer, respectively. Prolonged flush cycles shrink effective buffer reuse, elevating contention further and creating a self-reinforcing degradation loop that affects both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: Write timeout for X Plugin network communication.
entry.trigger_condition: A MySQL X Protocol write operation exceeds mysqlx_write_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The X Protocol network write operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL X Plugin system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when network data is not acknowledged, received, or written within the configured transport-level waiting window.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect packet loss, transport latency, client responsiveness, proxy behavior, and whether slow consumers or unstable links are delaying network progress.
